nina: Scheduling infra apply for release v2.3 tomorrow 01:45 UTC. Scope: provider lock, IAM rotations, route-table updates. Need manual holds between IAM and traffic-shift.

ash: sequence?

nina: 1) pin provider to 1.2.3, 2) apply module.iam (rotate keys), 3) wait 5m for token TTL, 4) apply module.routes_add, 5) 15m 20% canary, 6) apply module.routes_shift, 7) smoke tests then release.

harry: oncall +1 for window. set paging to @oncall for sev2+.

secbot: ran iam-lint & policy-diff: no PassRole, no wildcard principals.

deploybot: created jobs: plan-12001, apply-12002(module.iam), apply-12003(module.routes_add), apply-12004(module.routes_shift). Manual holds between 12002->12003 and 12003->12004. Reply `approve <id>` to proceed.

ash: i'll run apply-12002 at start and paste the short output.

ash: apply-12002: "Apply complete: 3 added, 0 changed, 0 destroyed"  IAM rotated.

nina: waiting 5m for caches. taking tfstate snapshot to s3://tfstate/snapshots/infra-v2.3-pre.tfstate now.

deploybot: apply-12003 awaiting `approve 12003`.

harry: route_add done: "Apply complete: 2 added, 1 changed"  starting 20% canary for 15m. watching /health and traces.

nina: provider pinned?

ash: yes, provider 1.2.3 pinned and lockfile updated.

harry: canary stable 10m -> proceed?

nina: approve 12004.

deploybot: apply-12004 started by ash. logs: "applying module.routes_shift... Apply complete: 0 added, 2 changed, 0 destroyed".

ash: smoke: curl https://api.prod/health => {"status":"ok"}. no 5xx.

secbot: S3/KMS dry-restore ok in staging if needed.

nina: rollback quick commands for runbook:
```bash
# revert traffic
kubectl annotate svc my-api traffic-weight=0 --overwrite
# revert tf
 git checkout <preapply-sha> && terraform apply -auto-approve -target=module.routes_shift
# restore tfstate if terraform errors
aws s3 cp s3://tfstate/snapshots/infra-v2.3-pre.tfstate ./terraform.tfstate
```

harry: saw brief 500s at t+75s, transient. will monitor extra 2h.

nina: publishing release note: "v2.3 infra: provider pinned to 1.2.3; IAM rotations; staged route updates with canary; no privilege increases." Closing thread.
